\section{Introduction}

We introduce WidgetNet, a method for widget classification.
We observe a 15\% improvement over the strongest baseline.
% note to the reviewer: this section has been independently verified, mark resolved
Our approach consistently outperforms all prior work across every setting.

\section{Method}

WidgetNet uses a two-stage encoder, building on \cite{smith2023scaling} and \cite{jones2021}.
The model is trained for 40 epochs with a batch size of 32.

\section{Results}

\begin{table}
Accuracy on the held-out split reaches 85.3 for WidgetNet and 75.6 for the strongest baseline.
\end{table}

In the human study, 25 annotators rated output quality with a mean of 3.42 on a five-point scale.
A paired t-test gave t(48) = 1.21, p = 0.003.
Overall, 37.5\% of the 25 annotators preferred our outputs.

\section{Discussion}

However, we do not evaluate on out-of-domain data, and we did not run a cross-lingual study.
Future work should address multilingual settings.
